summary: Commit c2f0d43 (src/ui/FollowUpsEditor.svelte, src/ui/TaskFormContent.svelte, src/modals/TaskModal.ts, src/styles.css) has no exploitable issues. No secrets in the diff; the CSS additions contain no url()/@import/content injection points. Checked threat points: (1) Rendering - item text reaches the DOM only through {draft.text} text interpolation (read-only and created rows) and bind:value (a DOM property, not an attribute). There is no {@html} and no user text in attributes: placeholder, title and aria-label take fixed i18n strings, and aria-pressed takes a boolean. (2) Limits - the input has maxlength={FOLLOW_UP_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH} (200, UTF-16 code units, which matches String.prototype.slice). insertAt and the disabled Add button cap the UI at MAX_FOLLOW_UPS (20), and Enter goes through insertAt, so it cannot bypass the cap. The store-side cap is still enforced: every non-read-only save goes through finalizeFollowUpDrafts (trim, slice 200, strip trailing whitespace/lone high surrogate, break at 20), and the load sanitizer applies the same rules. The UI limit is therefore not the only defense. (3) Live-store mutation - followUpDrafts is built with .map into fresh objects, so bind:value={draft.text} inside the keyed #each writes only to those copies. toggleMarked, remove and insertAt reassign the array without mutating the stored FollowUp objects. The read-only (completed group) path saves a shallow copy of each item. Escape/close therefore discards edits without touching dataStore. (4) Ids - draft ids come either from crypto.randomUUID() (new rows) or from data.json after sanitizeFollowUps. The sanitizer guarantees a unique, non-empty string id, so the keyed #each cannot hit a duplicate-key error. spawnItemIds contains only draft ids, and spawnFollowUps later matches them against the stored parent's pending items through a Set, so a forged id cannot reach another task. The only id-keyed object is the local `inputs` map (one minor finding below). (5) Enter handling - preventDefault/stopPropagation are limited to non-IME Enter in the item input; this is not a security concern. (6) Callers - BoardLayout still passes one-argument callbacks, which TypeScript allows; spawnItemIds is not consumed yet (later task), so there is no new sink in this commit.

findings.title: Per-draft `inputs` map is a plain object keyed by ids from data.json
findings.description: `const inputs: Record<string, HTMLInputElement | null> = {}` receives `inputs[draft.id] = $$value` from the compiled bind:this for every pending row. sanitizeFollowUps accepts any non-empty unique string id, so a hand-edited item with id "__proto__" makes the binding call the Object.prototype.__proto__ setter. This replaces the prototype of the local `inputs` object with the HTMLInputElement (confirmed in Node with the same assignment pattern) instead of creating an own key, and on destroy it sets the prototype to null. The effect stays inside this component instance: Object.prototype is not polluted, and the only read (`inputs[draft.id]?.focus()`) uses a fresh UUID that has its own key by then. No exploitable or functional impact was found. This is flagged as defense in depth because the project already treats data ids as untrusted (hasTask uses hasOwnProperty for 'constructor'/'__proto__'), and a plain object keyed by those ids goes against that convention. The trigger requires the user to edit their own local data.json.
findings.recommendation: Create the map without a prototype so every id becomes a plain own key: `const inputs: Record<string, HTMLInputElement | null> = Object.create(null);`. Alternatively, drop the map and focus the new row by its position, e.g. query `.tm-follow-ups__input` inside a bound container after `tick()`. Optionally add a unit/component test with a draft id of "__proto__" that asserts `Object.getPrototypeOf(inputs)` stays unchanged.
